content_text: Are nausea and vomiting making it difficult for you to eat? Don’t worry, it’s completely normal during the first trimester of pregnancy due to the physical and hormonal changes your body is going through. During this period, your levels of HCG and estrogen are adjusting to prepare your body for gestation. Additionally, nausea can be a result of increased sensitivity to smells and flavors, as well as psychological factors such as stress and anxiety. But don’t despair, there are ways to find relief! Here are some tips to help you alleviate nausea and improve your diet: - Regulate your portions: Eat small amounts of food rich in vitamins several times a day. - Snack between meals: Choose healthy and light snacks to satisfy your appetite. - Balance your plate: Make sure the portions of carbohydrates, fats, and sugars don’t exceed those of vegetables and fruits. - Salty crackers to the rescue: Try eating salty crackers to relieve nausea. Additionally, sucking on a piece of ice can help reduce this unpleasant sensation. - Stay hydrated: Drink liquids in small quantities consistently throughout the day. But avoid carbonated beverages! - Choose your foods wisely: Avoid strong-smelling foods that may trigger nausea. If possible, consume these foods fresh or at room temperature. Hot meals tend to intensify odors. - Take care of your oral hygiene: Brush your teeth after each meal and snack. This not only benefits your dental health but can also help prevent nausea. Remember, if your symptoms persist and are accompanied by pain, it’s important to consult your doctor for an accurate diagnosis. Don’t hesitate to seek help when you need it! Stay positive, you will soon overcome nausea and be able to enjoy a pleasant diet during your pregnancy!
